final_message:
I've stopped because the sandbox denied my `record_paper` call for Indurkar et al., and I don't want to work around that denial.

**What happened**
- Earlier `record_paper` calls ran normally. This one came back with "Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode".
- The read-only `read_pdf` call made in the same step went through, so only the write was blocked.
- The command was the same kind of literature-CLI call as before, so I don't know why it was refused. Rewording it or routing it through a different tool would amount to bypassing the block, so I haven't done that.

**Why I need it**
`record_paper` and `write_review` are my only outputs. Without them I can read papers but can't save the evidence-backed entries or the final review.

**Progress so far**
- **Dataset paper:** I couldn't open the PNAS or PMC PDFs with `read_pdf`. I read the Lumpe & Stankovic full text through the Europe PMC XML, so those details have no PDF page numbers.
  - Properties come from an Euler–Bernoulli FE beam homogenization with all structures scaled to ρ_rel ≈ 0.01. The base material is Es = 1 MPa, νs = 0.3, and the bar radius is 0.1 mm.
  - The paper's count is 2,730 + 14,532 − 135 − 40 = 17,087 entries. The 40 excluded had "very small members that cause numerical issues". That doesn't match our 17,262 catalog or the 41 flagged entries, so the catalog may be a different version.
  - The main text gives no value for C and no fitting procedure. Those are probably in the SI, which I haven't read.
- **Recorded:** only the Lumpe & Stankovic dataset entry.
- **Read but not recorded:**
  - Indurkar et al. 2022 (arXiv:2202.09427) trained a message-passing GNN on 17,201 lattices from this same catalog. It classified stretching vs bending with a 90:10 random split, reaching 95.2% train and 81.8% validation accuracy (92.27% for stretching vs non-stretching).
  - Grega et al. ICLR 2024 (arXiv:2401.16914) built an SE(3)-equivariant MACE model with a positive-semi-definite output layer, on a dataset derived from the same catalog. They reduced it to 8,954 base lattices and added nodal perturbations. I've read pages 1–6 of 25.

**How to proceed**
Please either allow the literature CLI commands in this session, or tell me if you'd rather I proceed another way. Once allowed, I'll record Indurkar and Grega, finish the remaining snowballing and full-text reads (Bastek, Zheng, Meyer, Kochmann, defect papers), and write the review.
